# Reading Ògún the way it was meant to be written
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *ogun*. This is the file on how **Ògún** replaced it.

Ògún's myths are the Yoruba meditation on power: the strength that clears the way for everyone, and the rage that, unmastered, turns on its own town. When the orisha first sought to descend to the earth, the primordial forest stood unbroken and none could pass — not Orunmila with his wisdom, not any god with any tool.  Ògún took his cutlass and cut the road through, and the gods followed him down — the mythic clearing of the way.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Ògún
- **ASCII form:** ogun
- **Meaning:** "God of iron"
- **Domain of influence:** Iron, War, Labour
- **Pantheon:** Yoruba
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** —
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 174 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

**Ògún** preserves its form without added diacritics: the restoration here is the exactness of the spelling itself, the form the tradition's own sources record. *ogun* and **Ògún** may look interchangeable to a search box; they are not interchangeable to a philologist.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Ògún** lives at [/sites/ogun/](/sites/ogun/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/ogun/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/ogun/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/ogun/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Ògún** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Defense, Military & Security** — War and iron are one craft in his cult; the cutlass that clears the road.
- **Manufacturing, Craft & Automation** — The iron master; every smithy and mechanics’ yard his chapel.
- **Communication, Messaging & Logistics** — The road-opener; infrastructure’s cutting edge, literally.

If a match here reads wrong, the atlas says how to challenge it. The patterns are falsifiable — that is what makes them worth publishing.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Yoruba tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Nigerian Studies — The Orisha Myths](/texts/nigerian-studies/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/ogun/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
